instruction: Start only after task 0008-intake-connectors-ai completes successfully. Conduct a deep, source-grounded diligence project for adding lawful native e-file capability to Folio. Use current IRS sources first: Publication 3112, Publication 1345, Publication 1436, Publication 4163, Publication 4164, Publication 5078, current MeF schemas/business rules, WSDL/status pages, ATS schedules, Authorized IRS e-file Provider requirements, EFIN/ETIN rules, Software Developer/Transmitter/ERO/Intermediate Service Provider roles, signature authorization and Form 8879 requirements, remote identity verification, security/WISP obligations, record retention, reject handling, acknowledgements, and state Fed/State MeF requirements through the Federation of Tax Administrators and representative states. Research practical launch paths: (A) Folio becomes IRS Software Developer plus Transmitter, while customer firms operate as EROs with their own EFINs; (B) Folio is Software Developer but uses an established authorized transmitter; (C) partner API only for tax packages where a compliant transmitter API actually exists. Explicitly determine which major return families can be supported through MeF for Folio's target practices, including 1040/1040-NR/1040-SS, 4868, 1041, 1065, 1120/1120-S, 7004, 94x, 1099/W-2/ACA where applicable, and state returns. Identify annual certification/testing burden, software IDs by tax year/package, security certificates/WSDL/SOR access, transmission protocols, operational monitoring, legal/compliance prerequisites, expected lead time, and what requires human IRS enrollment rather than code. Evaluate FreeTaxUSA's paid-preparer flow as a benchmark, but do not copy proprietary UI or code. Create docs/product/IRS_EFILE_DILIGENCE.md and docs/product/IRS_EFILE_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md with a decision matrix, recommended launch architecture, phased form-family rollout, compliance checklist, external approvals checklist, risk register, test/certification plan, build-vs-partner plan, and exact stop line between code we can build now and production transmission that must wait for authorization. Do not send any real tax return, do not access taxpayer data, do not claim IRS approval. Commit and push documentation to main. Do not deploy production.
